description:
No Nut November vs your prostate: what does the science actually say? Cyto breaks it down from the 6ix.

A 2025 meta-analysis pooled 29 studies (315,193 men). Higher ejaculation frequency was linked to lower prostate cancer risk (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77-0.90). Masturbation frequency alone was not significantly linked (OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.82-1.54), and most other sexual behaviours showed no significant link. A 2025 systematic review (10 studies) found the same pattern for intercourse (5-12+ times a month) but a possible risk increase with very frequent masturbation (2-7+ times a week) and more lifetime partners.

The catch: these are observational long-term habits, not a one-month challenge. Linked, not proven. Nothing here says a month of the challenge is harmful.

Sources (via PubMed):
Raeisvandi et al., BMC Cancer 2025 - https://doi.org/10.1186/s12885-025-15410-3
Firsty et al., Asian Pac J Cancer Prev 2025 - https://doi.org/10.31557/APJCP.2025.26.9.3193

Not medical advice. Men over 50 (or with family history) can ask their doctor about prostate screening.
